other_considerations.diagnosis: Insomnia due to major depressive disorder
other_considerations.note: Depression can cause sleep-onset or sleep-maintenance insomnia or early-morning waking; she denies depressive symptoms.
A significant life stressor can disturb sleep, with changes starting within 3 months of the event and resolving within about 6 months.
Stimulants such as cocaine and amphetamines raise sympathetic activity and can cause insomnia.
OSA often presents with insomnia symptoms, but she has had a tonsillectomy and is of normal weight, so it is unlikely.

x010: The note exam records DTRs '2+ and intact, and symmetric'; the SP is told to exhibit brisk reflexes and gold rank 3 cites 'Brisk DTRs'. The SP-simulated finding is the result (CONVERSION rule).
x011: SP-simulated only; the note exam does not mention a tremor.

source_issues: Caffeine amount differs: script p014 says 5 to 6 cups of coffee or energy drinks daily; the note says 4-5 cups of coffee per day; gold rank 2 says '4-5 cups of caffeine per day'. Patient fact f051 keeps the script.

Reflexes conflict: the SP is told to exhibit brisk reflexes and gold rank 3 cites 'Brisk DTRs', but the note exam records DTRs '2+ and intact, and symmetric' (e007). In v2 the simulated finding wins: the reflexes record (x010) reads 'Brisk deep tendon reflexes.'

The SP is told to show a fine tremor of the outstretched fingertips (x011), but the note exam does not mention it; the patient denies noticing any shaking (p015, f023), which is not necessarily a contradiction.

Gold rank 1 lists history items under exam findings ('Anxiety over academic achievement', 'No history of substance use'), and cites 'muscle tension', which the script does not support (she denies joint or muscle discomfort, p029).
Gold rank 1 'Impaired concentration' rests on the note HPI ('inability to concentrate'); the script (p008) only says she feels very sleepy in class and while driving. Added as note fact f015.
p022 asks about the last menstrual period, but the answer does not give it.
The challenging question has a doubled opening quotation mark in the source; cleaned.
notes: Oral contraceptive pills are one fact (f047) with sources p022, p023, and p031, to avoid paraphrase duplicates.
p018 is split: no general increase in sweating ('Not really', absent, f027) and wet palms most of the time (present, f028).

Note-only facts (v1 from_note): poor concentration (f015), lives with boyfriend (f067), no recent infection (f044), no sexual abuse (f068), no recent tragic events (f069). v1 'other' facts (sexual abuse, tragic events) map to social_background (safety/abuse, stressors).

'Look anxious and irritable' and the college worry are kept as acting notes; the note's own 'appears anxious and restless' is the general-appearance result (x005). The tremor and brisk reflexes the SP must show on examination are exam results (x011, x010).
The patient description 'average height and weight' is put in acting notes; the gold OSA rationale relies on it.

Conversion (v1 change): v1 kept both the note's normal reflexes (x011) and the SP's brisk reflexes (x013); per CONVERSION.md the simulated finding wins, so the single reflexes record says brisk and the conflict is in source_issues.

Conversion: sleep facts are split into the complaint f001 with duration, course, bedtime and routine children, hours of sleep (f006, with 'need 8 hours' child), night waking (f008, with 'trouble falling back asleep' child from p002), no waking before the alarm (f010) and alarm at 6 AM (f011). Palpitations (p017) are parent f024 with a coffee trigger child f025. Snoring (p007), caffeine (p014), alcohol (p036) and exercise (p013) have children.
Vitals: doorway values agree with the note ('HR: 102/minute, otherwise WNL', e002); one record per parameter citing both, marked initial.
Harmonisation pass: system general (sleep) for f001, f002, f003, f004, f005, f006, f007, f008, f009, f014.
